scientific_question: Can a seven-parameter cubic/cubic rational model trained below 700 K predict the highest-temperature observations of Hahn1, and does it outperform a cubic polynomial baseline?

data.name: NIST/ITL StRD Hahn1
data.reference: Hahn, T., NIST (1979), Copper Thermal Expansion Study
data.units_as_published: y is coefficient of thermal expansion; x is temperature in kelvin; no unit conversion or measurement uncertainty is invented

model.bounds: Unbounded coefficients as in the NIST model; denominator validity is checked separately and is never silently assumed
model.optimizer: scipy.optimize.curve_fit with identical settings and two starts; select the lowest training residual sum of squares

holdout_rule.purpose: Highest-temperature extrapolation with a stronger cubic-polynomial baseline, not only a linear baseline

full_fit_certification_rule.purpose: Separate known-answer reproduction against NIST, never used as holdout evidence

baselines: Ordinary least-squares linear response fitted only on x < 700
Ordinary least-squares cubic polynomial fitted only on x < 700
metrics: Training and holdout RMSE, MAE and maximum absolute residual
Holdout RMSE divided by training RMSE
Holdout RMSE compared with linear and cubic-polynomial baselines
Denominator signs and real roots over the experimental domain

decision_gate.limited_support: Holdout RMSE < 3 * training RMSE AND holdout RMSE < cubic-polynomial holdout RMSE
decision_gate.negative_or_unresolved: Otherwise report the rational model as not supported for this high-temperature task; do not retune on the 17 holdout points
decision_gate.interpretation: Passing is limited evidence for this single split, not a universal rational law, independent experimental replication or proof of parameter endogeneity

output_rule: Write validation/hahn1-high-temperature.json and papers/07_有理模型外推/fig07_hahn1_high_temperature.png; preserve all starts and negative results; refuse to overwrite existing results
prohibitions: No fitting or parameter selection on the 17 high-temperature observations
No claim that a rational fit proves a universal law or all seven parameters are physically endogenous
No claim that NIST certification is our independent thermal-expansion experiment
No hiding of denominator singularities, multiple minima or negative results
